transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-04
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording available: yes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Rivers (Bluehaven - Head of Partnerships), Lila Chen (Bluehaven - CTO), Tom Alvarez (Bluehaven - SA), Renee Park (Bluehaven - Security Lead, joined 00:28)

Auto-sumaries (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
- Intro + quick product positioning: Redwood inference runtime, Dedicated vs Private, cost controls.
- High-level partner goals: Bluehaven wants an edge-optimized inference path to bundle into their Accelerate appliance for telco/retail customers.
- Key constraints: VPC-onprem, strict data residency (EU for some customers), limited egress, SOC 2 requirements.
- Immediate asks: partner onboarding deck, benchmark plan, integration points for routing and billing.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Kim: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, AE here at Redwood Inference. With me is Priya Nair, our solutions eng. How's everyone doing?
00:08 Mark Rivers: Hi Alex, doing well. Thanks for setting this up. Mark here - Head of Partnerships at Bluehaven. Lila and Tom are on - thanks.
00:14 Lila Chen: Hi, yeah thanks. Quick FYI we've got a hard stop at 16:45 our time for another sync.
00:18 Priya Nair: Great, we'll be mindful. Quick agenda from our side: intro, high-level use cases, infra constraints, security + next steps. Sound okay?
00:26 Tom Alvarez: Yep, sounds good.
00:28 Renee Park: (joined) Sorry for the delay, Renee from security.
00:31 Alex Kim: No worries, Renee. Maybe quick round — Bluehaven share 30 seconds on the product and what you're hoping to achieve? Mark?
00:40 Mark Rivers: Sure, super quick — Bluehaven builds an "Edge Accelerator" appliance, it's a small rack unit that sits in telco central offices and in retail edge closets. Customers want to run LLM-powered features locally to avoid backhauling — especially for latency sensitive routing and retail checkout assistants. We're exploring bundling inference capabilities so partners can spin up models onsite.
01:03 Lila Chen: The other piece is we need a solution that supports multiple deployment modes: some customers will want fully on-prem KVMs, others VPC-connected but no customer data leaving region. So routing and data residency are huge.
01:18 Alex Kim: Understood — that's squarely in what Redwood's private and dedicated tiers are meant for. Priya, do you want to high-level the runtime?
01:25 Priya Nair: Yeah. So Redwood's serving runtime's optimized for continuous batching on GPUs, KV cache reuse, and it picks kernels based on model/sequence length. For edge we typically recommend smaller quantized model variants and a Dedicated pool per region to guarantee throughput. There's also a Private option where the control plane is in our cloud but runtime sits in your VPC, or fully private on-prem; both can be done.
01:48 Tom Alvarez: Quick question — when you say KV cache is reused, do you mean across sessions or per model instance? I'm worried about memory starve on our small boxes.
01:55 Priya Nair: Good call — it's per instance but we do prefix caching to avoid recomputing tokens for repeated prompts; on smaller hardware you can tune cache retention and we can set eviction policies. Also quantization profiles reduce memory footprint.
02:10 Mark Rivers: And how do you handle routing? Like can we route requests to a local edge box and fallback to a regional Redwood Dedicated cluster if capacity's hit?
02:18 Alex Kim: Yes, smart routing is a core capability — policy based routing by latency, cost, region. Fallbacks to compatible model variants are supported. There is a small latency penalty for fallback but it keeps services online.
02:30 Lila Chen: What's the typical latency for local runs — ballpark for a 2K token chat for a quantized 13B?
02:36 Priya Nair: Ballpark, on an A10-ish class edge GPU maybe 120-250ms per response chunk depending on sequence; on high-end A40/V100 variants lower. That's speculative — we'll need concrete benchmarks.
02:49 Tom Alvarez: We'll definitely need a benchmark plan. Our product team has SLOs of <200ms tail for checkout flows.
02:56 Alex Kim: Notes noted — we'll produce a bench plan.
03:00 Mark Rivers: Security — Renee, any immediate callouts? Renee?
03:04 Renee Park: Hi — thanks. Our customers are enterprise telcos, so SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 posture is expected. We also need audit logs for inference requests, SAML SSO for partner ops, and KMS integration for key storage. Also some customers insist on BYOK/HSM.
03:20 Alex Kim: That aligns with Redwood Private — we support KMS integrations, HSM for enterprise, and audit logs in the console. We'll share our security pack. There might be a couple of redactions in auto transcribed docs, but we'll attach the security PDF.
03:33 Lila Chen: For data residency — some customers will not allow cross-border egress. Can we guarantee regional lock?
03:39 Priya Nair: Yes, we can pin runtime to a region and enforce routing. For fully on-prem customers it's a non-issue since data never leaves. For hybrid ones, we can set policy to never fallback outside the region unless explicitly allowed.
03:52 Mark Rivers: Pricing model question — how would we bundle this? Licensing per device? Per token? Some of our customers prefer per-device perpetual and some prefer consumption.
04:02 Alex Kim: We have flexible models — for Dedicated/reserved capacity we do committed throughput pricing; for Hosted it's usage-per-token. For partnerships we often do a hybrid: per-device seat + committed capacity for pilot then settle on per-token or per-device for scale. We'll share a pricing guardrail doc.
04:18 Tom Alvarez: Integration surface — what's the overhead to embed the Redwood SDK into our management plane? We have an onboard service that provisions devices and wants to orchestrate model rollouts.
04:26 Priya Nair: We expose REST SDKs and webhooks; model rollouts can be controlled via API; for edge you'll want a small agent that handles model pulls, KV cache warm-up, and health checks. We can share a sample agent repo.
04:40 Mark Rivers: Excellent. A few practical constraints from our ops folks: egress is capped on many telco sites to 5Mbps, so we need to avoid frequent fallbacks. Also power/cooling limits mean we may prioritize smaller quantized models.
04:55 Priya Nair: Good notes — that argues for aggressive prefix caching and local routing so fallbacks are rare. We'll include those in benchmarking metrics.
05:06 Lila Chen: On model support — do you onboard custom fine-tuned models? Some customers will want to run their own proprietary models.
05:13 Priya Nair: Yes, we can host customer models, and you can bring your own. There are constraints for certain proprietary LLM formats but we support many standard formats and can help with conversion/quantization. We'll need access to a sanitized sample to test.
05:27 Mark Rivers: Any regulatory issues with running customer models through Redwood control plane? Some customers want zero cloud control plane telemetry.
05:34 Alex Kim: We can offer a private control plane or fully on-prem package to satisfy that. The private control plane can also be deployed in customer-managed VPC.
05:44 Tom Alvarez: Does Redwood provide billing APIs so we can surface usage to our customers and do revenue share?
05:49 Alex Kim: Yep — we have metering and billing exports, and can integrate with partner revenue share flows. We'll need to define the contract though.
05:57 Renee Park: Quick security Q — how granular is your RBAC for partner ops? We need per-customer, per-device scopes.
06:03 Priya Nair: We support RBAC at route/token levels and can restrict model access per tenant. We'll share docs for RBAC roles.
06:12 Mark Rivers: Can you give a short walkthrough of an example topology? Like a telco site with our edge box and Redwood Dedicated in region and fallback rules?
06:19 Priya Nair: Yes — quick verbal sketch: edge box hosts runtime with local model variant; agent reports health to your mgmt plane; requests try local runtime first; if local capacity exceeded or model mismatch, router tries regional Dedicated pool within same region; if that fails and policy allows, fall back to a lower-cost hosted model in another region.
06:44 Alex Kim: I'll drop a topology sketch in the follow-up.
06:47 Mark Rivers: Thanks. Deep dive ask — Tom, Lila, can we agree on two pilot customers (one telco, one retail) to run an initial 6-week pilot? We want to see throughput and tail latency.
06:59 Tom Alvarez: Yes, we have a retail proof-of-concept lined up in Q1. I'd like the telco candidate too.
07:05 Lila Chen: We'll confirm names after internal sync, but counts as yes in principle.
07:10 Alex Kim: Great. Bench specifics — Priya, can you outline what metrics we'll measure?
07:16 Priya Nair: Sure: tail latency (p95/p99), per-request cost, failure rate during fallbacks, memory utilization, model load times, and KV cache hit ratio. We'll also monitor network egress and error traces.
07:30 Mark Rivers: Will Redwood instrument traces in our console or do we need to integrate with our APM?
07:36 Priya Nair: We can push traces to your APM or use Redwood Console for per-route dashboards. For an integration pilot, we usually enable both.
07:46 Renee Park: We need to review your SOC 2 report and pen test summaries before pilot.
07:51 Alex Kim: Absolutely — I'll attach the security packet.
07:53 Mark Rivers: Are there any gotchas around model licensing? Some open models have license terms restricting commercial use.
07:59 Priya Nair: We'll vet model licenses during onboarding; for commercial features we'll often recommend commercially licensed variants or have customers bring licensed models.
08:10 Tom Alvarez: Question on quantization — do you handle INT8 or lower and do you support FP16 fallbacks?
08:16 Priya Nair: We support multiple quantization profiles including INT8 and custom lower-bit profiles depending on kernel support. FP16 is supported on most modern GPUs. We'll advise per-model.
08:27 Mark Rivers: Any initial lift estimate for integrating the agent? Our platform team prefers things in under 4 weeks for a pilot.
08:34 Alex Kim: For a minimal pilot we can have a PoC in 3-4 weeks: onboarding, model push, basic agent, and a small bench harness. Priya will own the technical plan.
08:44 Priya Nair: I'll draft a 3-week sprint plan and share timeline items.
08:48 Lila Chen: About billing — for pilot, we want invoicing consolidations and usage CSVs.
08:54 Alex Kim: We'll provide consolidated billing and CSV exports; can do invoice consolidation for partner accounts.
08:59 Mark Rivers: Great. Any other open concerns?
09:02 Tom Alvarez: One more — fallback cost visibility. We need to ensure customers can see when fallbacks happen and what cost was incurred so they can build rules.
09:12 Priya Nair: We'll include fallback logs in the console and add an alert you can surface to customers.
09:18 Mark Rivers: Ok that's helpful.
09:20 Alex Kim: Cool. Quick recap and assignables then wrap, we have about 30 minutes left but want to confirm next steps.
09:28 Alex Kim: Recap: Alex sends partner deck + security pack; Priya shares benchmark plan and agent sample; Bluehaven confirms pilot customers and shares network/egress constraints plus topology. We schedule a technical deep dive week of Nov 17. Anything to add?
09:45 Lila Chen: Add Renee to the security deep-dive invite.
09:49 Alex Kim: Done. Anything else?
09:52 Mark Rivers: Nothing here, appreciate the time.
09:55 Alex Kim: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and links.
09:58 Tom Alvarez: Thanks, bye.
10:00 Meeting end.
